title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 14
paragraphs: The Persians, hearing this, rejoiced and made obeisance. But when night came on, the same dream came once more and stood over Xerxes as he lay asleep and said: “Son of Darius, it seems then that you have openly renounced the expedition in the assembly of the Persians, and taken no account of my words, as if you had heard them from no one at all. Now be well assured of this: unless you march at once, this will be the result for you — just as you became great and mighty in a short time, so you will be brought low again, quickly.”
